subject: DPA preflight: subprocessor map, transfer mechanism & e-sign preference for ClearBank pilot
messages:
From: Nora Blake <nora.blake@clearbank.com>

Cc: Matthew Li <matthew.li@clearbank.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:21:00 +0100
Subject: DPA request and subprocessor list for upcoming pilot

Hi Sofia,

We’re gearing up for the pilot next month and need a few items to finish legal intake: 1) your most recent DPA template, 2) a full list of subprocessors with country locations, and 3) confirmation of the cross-border transfer mechanism you rely on (SCCs, UK adequacy, or another basis). Also—do you have a preferred e-sign provider? ClearBank tends to use DocuSign but can accommodate AdobeSign if needed.

If you could send the materials and a short note on any standard redlines you accept, that will help speed review on our side. Target timeline: signature before the pilot starts (week of 6/21).

Thanks,
Nora Blake
Head of GDPR
ClearBank

Attachments: none
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.inference.com>
To: Nora Blake <nora.blake@clearbank.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA request and subprocessor list for upcoming pilot

Hi Nora — thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached our current DPA template (Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.docx) and the latest subprocessor mapping (subprocessor_list_2026-06.csv). Quick summary:

- Transfer mechanism: for EU<->US flows we operate on our standard EU SCCs (we can provide the executed annex) and for UK customers we rely on the UK international data transfer provisions; where customers prefer, we can execute the SCCs in-line with the DPA.
- Subprocessors: locations and primary function are in the CSV; we maintain SOC2 Type II for core infra providers — links and attestations below.
- E-sign: DocuSign is our default; we support AdobeSign on request.
- Redlines: we typically accept non-material edits to Sections 2–5 (data purpose/retention/security) but we don’t alter core liability caps or data residency commitments without legal escalation.

Next steps: Laura (Legal) is looped for any redline questions; Karthik will coordinate the commercial timeline. If DocuSign works for you, we’ll prepare the envelope and send a PowerForm link.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments (stubs): Redwood_DPA_Template_v1.docx (attachment), subprocessor_list_2026-06.csv (attachment)
From: ClearBank Legal <legal@clearbank.com>

Cc: Matthew Li <matthew.li@clearbank.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 08:11:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPA request and subprocessor list for upcoming pilot

Sofia — thanks for the quick reply and the files. A couple of follow-ups from our side:

1) We see a subprocessor listed in the US that handles logging/metrics (listed as "TelemetryCo" in the CSV). Please confirm whether telemetry logs may contain personal data, and if so, whether logs are pseudonymized/hashed prior to ingestion.
2) Can you provide SOC2 links or a short attestation for the infra providers? We typically request the latest SOC2 report or a scoped attestation.
3) Section 7 in your template (Limitation of Liability) looks standard, but our counsel may propose a narrow exception for negligence that we consider material. Are you open to a single redline on that section?

Also, DocuSign is preferable for us.

On timelines, we can review and turn comments in 48–72 hours once we have the SOC2/attestation and the clarified subprocessor note.

Regards,
ClearBank Legal Team
legal@clearbank.com

Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 12:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA request and subprocessor list for upcoming pilot

Hi Nora / Legal Team — replying with the details requested and a suggested path forward.

1) TelemetryCo (US) — function: aggregated metrics and observability. We do not send raw user messages to TelemetryCo; logs include timestamps, request IDs, and aggregated counters. Any identifiers included are pseudonymized (hashed) before export. I’ve noted the relevant fields in the attached CSV.

2) SOC2/Attestation — Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II; we don’t publish the full report publicly but can provide a scoped attestation PDF and a read-only link to the report on request under NDA. For now, here are the attestation snippets (summary): status=SOC2 Type II, last audit=2026-03, scope=serving runtime + infra.

3) Liability redline — we are open to discussion. To keep execution timelines short for the pilot, we typically accept a limited carve-out that narrows wording rather than expanding cap amounts. I’ve attached a redline (redline_dpa_v2.docx) with the proposed compromise language that keeps the cap but clarifies negligence language.

Proposed next steps:
- If DocuSign is the preference, we will prepare the envelope and include the redline in the DocuSign package so you can accept/decline specific changes inline.
- We aim to have the envelope out within 24 hours of your confirmation.
- Once signed, we will provide the SOC2 attestation PDF and a pipeline for on-demand subprocessor attestations.

Linking HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1942

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you prefer to go line-by-line.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference
